div.head: III Atr 4
div.ab: Gif se hlaford þonne hine ladian wylle mid twam godum þegenum, þæt he næfre þeofgild né gúlde, siððan þæt gemót wæs on Brómdune, ne he betihlod nære, gange tó anfealdum órdale oððe gilde IIIgilde.

Si dominus tunc uelit eum purgare cum duobus bonis tainis, quod numquam furigildum reddidit, postquam concilium fuit apud Bromdonam, nec accusatus fuerit, uadat ad triplex ordalium uel persoluat triplum.
Gif se hlaford þonne hine ladian wylle mid twam godum þegenum, þæt he næfre þeofgild né gúlde, siððan þæt gemót wæs on Brómdune, ne he betihlod nære, gange tó anfealdum órdale oððe gilde IIIgilde.

Wenn [dessen] Herr mit zwei guten Thegnas ihn jedoch reinigen will, dass jener, seitdem der Reichstag zu ‘Bromdun’ war, weder jemals Diebesstrafe gezahlt habe, noch bescholten worden sei, schreite jener [nur] zu einfachem Ordale oder zahle dreifach.

But if [his] lord will clear him with two good thegns, [swearing] that he has never paid theft-compensation since the assembly at ‘Bromdun’, nor been of bad repute, let him go [only] to the single ordeal or pay threefold.

If, however, his lord is willing to clear him, [swearing], along with two good thegns, that he has neither been convicted of theft nor been accused since the assembly was held at Bromdun, he shall go to the simple ordeal or pay threefold [the value of the goods involved].

If, however, the lord is willing to clear him, along with two good thegns, that he never paid compensation for theft since the assembly was held at Bromdun nor was accused, he is to go to the simple ordeal or to pay three-fold.
div.note: Quadr.'s ‘triplex’ is wrong (H ‘anfealdum’, single); Liebermann leaves it as printed. H's ‘betihlod’ should be ‘betihtlod’. Liebermann compares I Atr 1.2–1.3.; AP: corrected against Whitelock p. 445, October 2026 (was “If, however, the lord is willing to clear him, along with two good thegns, that he never paid compensation for theft since the assembly was held at Bromdun nor was accused, he is to go to the simple ordeal or to pay three-fold.”, now “If, however, the lord is willing to clear him, along with two good thegns, that he never paid compensation for theft since the assembly was held at Bromdun nor was accused, he is to go to the simple ordeal or to pay three-fold. (expanded letters in italics: Bromdun)”)

note.seg: Der Satz setzt 3, 4 fort.—H liest gegen Q richtig, laut I Atr und weil offenbar der letzthin Unbescholtene besser behandelt werden soll als der Bescholtene. Der Irrtum Q's entstand durch das folgende triplum

This sentence continues 3, 4. — H reads correctly against Q, in accordance with I Atr and because the man who has latterly been of good repute is evidently to be treated better than the man of ill repute. Q's error arose from the triplum that follows
Also leichter als 3, 4, gemäss leichterem Ordal
Thus lighter than 3, 4, in accordance with the lighter ordeal
Q has vadat ad triplex ordalium which is probably incorrect in view of I Atr. 1, 3.

note.label: Bromdun
note.seg: Too common a name for identification. Brandon in Norkolk, Suffolk, Warwickshire, Durham, all go back on this form, as also does Brendon, Devon, Bromden, Shropshire, Brundon, Suffolk.
